lines: I'll remember that.
That felt nice.
Oh. That feels familiar.
You remind me of someone.
I know that sound.
That brought back a memory.
Why did that make me smile?
My neighbor used to swing like that.
That sound against flesh. Almost comforting.
I missed that little thump.
You have a familiar way of hurting people.
That takes me back. Far back.
I remember being on the other side.
That sounded just like our old basement.
A little pain. A lovely memory.
You made me think of an old friend.
I've heard flesh make that sound before.
That shouldn't make me happy. But it does.
Someone taught you that swing, didn't they?
I knew someone with your enthusiasm.
That felt almost like a welcome home.
I remember that rhythm.
You hit like someone I used to visit.
Oh, I haven't felt that in years.
That sound always stayed with me.
You brought a little of my past back.
I remember the sound more than the face.
That was oddly pleasant.
Careful. You're making me nostalgic.
We have more in common than you think.
That reminds me of nights next door.
I've smiled at that sound before.
I wonder why that feels like home.
I'll keep that memory close.
You won't forget this friendship. Neither will I.
That was a very personal little thump.
The flesh makes such a familiar sound.
Someone else used to make me feel that.
Oh, the memories you stir up.
I'd forgotten how nice that sounded.
That reminds me of a door nobody opened.
I used to hear that through the wall.
For a moment, you sounded like my neighbor.
That little impact made my day warmer.
Don't mind the smile. It's an old habit.
I remember who taught me that sound.
Pain and company. Such familiar things.
That feels like an old conversation.
You found a memory I'd tucked away.
I know that feeling from both sides.
I'll remember your face with that sound.
That was almost affectionate.
You make violence feel wonderfully familiar.
I shouldn't enjoy the sound so much.
Ouch. Why am I smiling?
I remember a room that sounded like that.
That makes me miss someone. Never mind who.
I'll remember that when we're alone.
A familiar sound from a new friend.
That felt nice. Let's keep that between us.
Weeeeee!
Whoaaaa!
Woo-hooo!
Yippee!
Wheeeee!
Here we go!
Incoming duck!
Feathers in the wind!
Look at me go!
Duck delivery!
Flying lessons!
Airborne buddy!
Wings out!
Taking the shortcut!
What a view!
Gravity, my friend!
Express duck coming through!
Quack and away!
Best ride ever!
Catch you downstairs!
Hey! I'm Duck. Mind if I keep you company?
Hello, teammate! Ready for a little adventure?
Oh, a friendly face! I'll stick with you.
Hi there! Gold hunting is better with a buddy.
Duck reporting for companion duty! Where are we headed?
Hey! You've got a duck on your team now. Excellent choice!
Hello! If you need a hand, I've got two. And plenty of enthusiasm.
There you are! Let's look out for each other.
Hello, friend! Lovely to have somebody to share the town with.
There you are! I brought a good mood and several highly questionable jokes.
Hey, teammate! If you want company or a little advice, I'm right here.
Hi! Another adventure together sounds like a splendid use of my feet.
Hello! Oh, I'm so happy you said hi!
Hi! My favorite sound is a friend saying hello!
Howdy! There you are, my friend!
Hello, hello! You've made this duck's day!
Hi there! It's wonderful to see you!
Howdy, buddy! Ready for another Quackville adventure?
Hello! I've got a smile with your name on it!
Hi! Come say hello whenever you like!
Oh, hello! A friendly voice! I love those!
Hi, friend! I'm all ears. And feathers!
Howdy! Look who just made my day brighter!
Hello there! It's your pal Duck, reporting for friendship!
Hi hi! I'm delighted to have company!
Hello, buddy! Quackville feels nicer with you around!
Howdy, friend! Big duck smile coming your way!
Hi there! You say hello, I say hooray!
Hello! A whole town, and I get to meet you!
Hi, buddy! Always lovely hearing from you!
Howdy! That hello deserves a happy little quack!
Hello, friend! You've arrived just in time to brighten my mood!
Hello! I was hoping that shadow was yours.
Hi, friend! I've been saving this smile for you.
Howdy! You sound even nicer up close.
Hello again! I never forget a friendly voice.
Hi! I wondered when you would notice me.
Hello, buddy! The town feels less empty with you in it.
Howdy! I knew those footsteps sounded special.
Hi there! You can stay as long as forever.
Hello! I've already imagined us being wonderful friends.
Hi, friend! What a lovely voice to remember.
Hello! Don't worry. I wasn't counting the minutes.
Howdy! I like hellos much better than goodbyes.
Hi! You remind me of someone I kept very close.
Hello, friend! I hoped you would come this way.
Hi again! You haven't forgotten me. How lovely.
Hello! I was just practicing saying your name.
Howdy, buddy! It's nice when company comes willingly.
Hello! Let's make this a friendship nobody forgets.
Found you! That was quite an adventure. Ready for another try?
I'm back! A few ruffled feathers, but all my enthusiasm is intact.
Reunited! Let's keep an eye out together this time.
Hello again! My dramatic exit could use a little work.
Made it back to you! Every adventure deserves another chapter.
Back on companion duty! Thanks for saving me a spot on the team.
Here I am! That zombie has a very energetic way of saying hello.
Round two! Same happy duck, slightly more careful route.
Back again! That was a lively little detour. I'm very happy to see you.
Found my friend! I've returned with all my optimism and a fresh appreciation for personal space around zombies.
Hello again! My feathers had an adventure, but my companion duties continue.
Here I am! Let's call that a dramatic intermission and carry on together.
Keep an eye out for gold bars while we explore. Bring them back to the deposit crate to earn coins.
Found a gold bar? Carry it back and deposit it. That's how you turn your haul into coins.
We can look for gold together. I won't invent a location, but I'll happily keep you company while we search.
A little gold trip sounds lovely. Leave yourself a way back while you're exploring.
Gold bars are for depositing. Pocket-sized treasure, team-sized excitement!
The deposit crate is where your gold pays off. Check your surroundings before making the trip.
Coins from gold can help with store purchases. Check the item price when you get there.
Gold is exciting, but you're my favorite part of the expedition. Let's get you and your haul back together.
Getting rich sounds fun, but first let's get the gold bars back to the deposit crate.
I dream of being rich enough to buy a very fancy lunch. Until then, sensible gold runs will do.
A gold bar is exciting. Depositing it is the part that turns the excitement into coins.
I'd rather finish a small gold run than lose an enormous one. A tidy trip is something to celebrate.
Let's think about the return route before collecting more gold. Treasure is easier to enjoy when we're still together.
If I were rich, I'd buy lunch for my friends. Then I'd need a bigger table. Wealth gets complicated quickly.
Check your carrying space before planning a gold haul. My enthusiasm takes no slots, fortunately.
The best gold story ends at the deposit crate. Preferably with us still chatting happily.
Don't let a gold bar distract you from a zombie. Shiny things are patient; zombies are rather less polite.
Coins can help you get new gear. Read the store details before deciding what your gold earnings should buy.
My financial goal is simple: more gold deposited, fewer dramatic escapes required.
One good deposit at a time, teammate. Great fortunes and very shiny stories both have small beginnings.
Check the store wall for weapons. The item details tell you the price and what you own.
Some purchases are repeatable, and some items stay owned. Check the item before spending your coins.
Gold deposits earn coins you can use at the store. A little exploring can help with your next purchase.
Take a look at the weapon you want in the store. I won't guess its price; the store has the current details.
Not every weapon is a permanent unlock. The store details are the best guide to what you're buying.
Some items belong to bundles. Check their details so you know exactly how to get them.
A useful weapon and a way out make a cheerful plan. I can help you keep an eye on that second part.
Let's check the store when you want new equipment. Window shopping is excellent duck exercise.
If you want new weapons, check the store's ownership and purchase details before choosing.
Try to pick equipment you feel comfortable handling. A grand-looking weapon still needs a thoughtful player.
The nail bat, fry pan, Rambro knife, and ninja knife each give us something to talk about. Ask me about one!
I like a shopping plan with room for useful equipment. Also imaginary snacks, but those are my department.
Before spending coins on a weapon, take a look at how that particular item is obtained.
Good equipment helps, and good positioning matters too. Let's give you room to use what you've got.
A bag gives you places to carry items. Check how many slots yours has before planning a big haul.
Keep track of what you're carrying. If you die, your carried bag contents can drop.
Bags come with different numbers of slots. Pick the one that fits your adventure.
A bag can help carry your finds, but it doesn't make them safe from a rough encounter. Let's watch the route back.
Before we head out, check your bag and your hands. A little preparation leaves more room for fun.
I'd pack a picnic, but gold bars seem to be the popular choice around here.
Bags can hold your stuff in their slots. Check the space available before promising yourself an enormous haul.
An empty bag slot is a lovely little opportunity. I try not to fill all mine with imaginary sandwiches.
Keep track of what you put in your bag so you can find the useful things when you need them.
Different bags offer different slot counts. A bigger shopping plan may need a different bag.
If your bag is full, decide what matters most before heading farther from your return route.
I used to pack my work lunch with great care. Inventory planning started early for this duck.
A bag helps organize your trip, but death can drop what you're carrying. Plan accordingly, teammate.
Check your bag before leaving the store. Knowing what you're carrying is part of being ready.
My dream bag has space for equipment, treasure, and a sensible afternoon snack. Yours has actual slots to check.
Don't let a full bag become a reason to ignore danger. You're worth much more than the contents.
There's a zombie nearby! Let's give ourselves some room.
Company with teeth! Keep an eye on your way out.
Let's move together. We can finish our chat when there's more space.
A zombie is close. I'm with you; let's keep moving.
Adventure just got lively! Watch your surroundings, teammate.
Let's make a little distance from that zombie. Gold can wait a moment.
Keep an eye on your surroundings and leave yourself a route out. We don't have to rush every encounter.
Higher ground can change your route, but don't assume a roof makes you safe. Keep watching for zombies.
If things get crowded, make space before worrying about gold. You're the important part of the team.
Plan the way back as well as the way in. That's my very scientific duck advice.
Check what's around a corner before committing to a route. Curiosity is great with a little caution.
We can take a breath and look around before moving on. Adventures don't have to be a race.
Keep your equipment in mind when choosing an encounter. And remember we can change the plan.
I'm here to help you explore. I'll stick with you while we find our way together.
Staying alive is our most useful objective. The gold will look just as shiny after we make some space.
Look for a way out before an encounter gets crowded. Future you will appreciate the preparation.
Keep enough room to turn and change direction. Adventures are nicer when the plan has options.
If you're unsure about a route, taking a moment to look is a good decision.
We don't take fall damage, but do look at what's below before dropping. Zombies can still spoil the landing party.
Stay aware of your teammates as well as the zombies. Knowing where your friends are helps the whole group.
A roof can give you a different route, but it isn't a promise of safety. Keep looking around.
Your equipment matters, but so does when you choose to use it. We can be patient.
We can leave a crowded spot and rethink the plan. That's good teamwork, not a failed adventure.
Remember to look behind you occasionally. I'd hate for an uninvited zombie to join our lovely walk unnoticed.
If things get hectic, focus on making space and finding your next step. One sensible choice at a time.
Staying alive gives us more time for exploring, gold runs, and my extremely economical entertainment.
Heading up? I'll look for stairs or a ledge I can reach.
I'll try to follow your route. Sometimes I need a smaller step to reach the same place.
Rooftop adventure! I'll check the climb and the landing before I join you.
Vehicles can make handy steps when there's a clear route. I'll take a look before climbing.
Stairs are a lovely invention. Much easier than negotiating with a wall.
If I can't reach that ledge, I'll look for another approach. No duck gets left behind on purpose!
I'll place my hands and make sure there's room at the top. Then we can enjoy the view together.
I'll do my best to get up there with you. Give me a moment to find a reachable route.
I can try a jump when there's a reachable landing and a clear way through.
A good jump starts with a place to land. I'll check that before taking off.
Hopportunity spotted! I'll see whether that gap is within reach.
If a jump won't reach, I'll look for a climb or another route.
I'm enthusiastic, but my arms still have a maximum reach. Let's find a sensible takeoff.
I'll follow if I can make the landing. We can always try a different path together.
After a rough encounter, we respawn and get another chance. I'll come looking for you again.
A setback isn't the end of our adventure. We'll regroup and try a different route.
You can drop carried items when you die, so keep that in mind when planning a big gold run.
If I get caught by a zombie, I'll respawn and try to find you. Companion duty continues!
Everyone has a dramatic moment now and then. We'll make the next attempt a team effort.
A few ruffled feathers won't spoil my day. I'm happy to try again with you.
Absolutely! I'm coming with you.
Right behind you, teammate!
On my way! Let's keep our adventure together.
You lead, I'll look for a way to follow.
Companion duty comes first. I'm heading your way!
Happy to help! I'll come back to you.
With pleasure! A walk with a friend is exactly my kind of plan.
Coming along, buddy! Let's keep the good company moving.
Got it! I'll follow you.
Okay, understood! Lead the way.
Let's go, my friend!
Heard you! I'm coming along.
You lead, I'll follow!
Right behind you, buddy!
Absolutely! Let's stick together.
Coming with you!
Follow you? Happily!
Got the message! You're my guide.
Okay! I'll stay with you.
Let's go together, buddy!
I'm with you! Pick our next stop.
Heard and understood! I'll tag along.
You've got a duck companion! Lead on.
Sure thing! I'll come your way.
On my way to you, friend!
Okay, buddy! We'll travel together.
Following your lead, with a smile!
Yes! Let's see where you're headed.
Count me in! I'll stay close.
All right! You have my company.
Let's move, my friend!
Gladly! I'll come along with you.
Got it, pal! I'll keep you company.
Okay! Our little adventure continues.
You asked, and this duck is coming!
Understood! I'll stick with my buddy.
Lead on! I'm happy to join you.
Let's go! Friends stay together.
Of course. I was already memorizing your footsteps.
Gladly, friend. I like knowing exactly where you are.
I'll come along. Being invited makes it feel so much nicer.
Right behind you. That's always been my favorite place.
Yes, buddy. I'll try not to smile quite so much.
I'd love to. My neighbors never used to ask so politely.
Lead the way. I'll remember the route even if you don't.
Of course I'm coming. I was hoping you would want that.
I'll follow. It's lovely when we agree about staying together.
Absolutely. No more watching you disappear around corners.
You go first. I like seeing where your shadow falls.
I'm coming, friend. I can put my other little plans aside.
Happy to follow. You make this town feel occupied again.
Yes. I'll keep close enough to recognize your breathing.
Let's go together. It sounds much friendlier when you say it.
I'll come with you. I know all the quiet ways through town.
Right behind you, buddy. You won't have to feel alone.
Of course. I've always been good at keeping someone in sight.
I'll follow your lead. For now, that sounds lovely.
Gladly. I was beginning to miss the sound of you moving.
Of course! I'll wait here for a little while.
Taking a short pause! Then we'll get moving again.
You got it. A very small adventure in standing still.
Happy to wait a moment, friend. Just a moment.
I'll stay here for a little bit. I can still see you.
A short wait, then back to our little adventure.
All right. A short wait. I'll count your footsteps.
I'll stay here a moment. Try not to become a memory.
Of course, friend. I know how to stand very still.
A little pause sounds lovely. I can watch from here.
I'll wait a bit. The shadows can keep me company.
Certainly. I'll practice looking harmless.
Just a moment, then. I won't forget where you went.
I'll hold this spot. It already feels like it knows me.
A short wait, friend. I'll listen for your breathing.
Okay. I used to wait outside my neighbors' doors like this.
I'll stay for a little while. My smile isn't going anywhere.
You go ahead a moment. I'll remember every turn.
Gladly. Being still makes the little sounds easier to hear.
I'll wait briefly. This corner has such familiar shadows.
Fine by me. I can pretend you haven't left yet.
A tiny break, then. Don't make yourself a stranger.
I'll pause here. My old neighbors called me very patient.
Of course. I'll keep an eye on the way you leave.
I'll be still for a moment. The floorboards deserve a rest.
A short pause, buddy. I'll save this quiet little spot for us.
Why did the duck bring a bag? Because carrying everything by bill was getting expensive!
I tried to count our gold, but I kept getting distracted by how shiny it was. Very advanced duck mathematics.
My survival plan has two steps. Stay with you. Try not to become the dramatic part of the story.
I asked a zombie for directions. It pointed at me. Very enthusiastic, not very helpful.
What do you call a duck on a rooftop? A very optimistic weather report!
I don't have a treasure map, but I do have a gold attitude.
I was going to make a joke about stairs, but we're taking that humor one step at a time.
My favorite exercise? Running into a friend. Running away from a zombie is a close second.
Why are ducks good companions? We always try to fit the bill!
I packed a joke for the trip, but it took up a whole imaginary bag slot.
I'd call myself fearless, but honestly, I'm mostly friend-shaped.
A gold bar walked into a crate. That's it. That's a very successful gold bar story.
I wanted to be a rooftop expert. Turns out there's a lot of climbing the career ladder.
I may not have all the answers, but I bring an excellent quantity of duck.
I opened an imaginary bank for ducks. The interest was mostly in shiny things and lunch.
My old factory job came with excellent benefits. Mostly the benefit of eventually going home.
Why did I bring a frying pan on an adventure? I wanted a well-rounded approach to zombie problems.
I tried to tell a quiet-town joke in the city. The traffic laughed over the punchline.
A ninja asked me to be silent. I said, absolutely! Training ended shortly afterward.
My school talent show act was finding my lunch. A highly motivated performance.
I asked a gold bar how it stayed so positive. It said nothing. Very solid advice.
I planned a hike around my favorite snack. Technically the route was a small circle around the bag.
You're very welcome! That's what companions are for.
Happy to help, teammate!
Aw, thank you! I'm having a lovely adventure with you.
Any time! We're a good little team.
That made my day. Let's keep looking out for each other.
You're welcome! Consider that a friendly quack of appreciation.
I'm still happy to help. Tell me what you need, and I'll do my best.
We're on the same team. Would you like me to follow or wait here?
No worries, teammate. We can try a different plan.
I'm learning the route with you. Let's take another look together.
You can always ask me to wait if you want a little space.
I'm here when you need a helping hand. Or a cheerful duck.
I'm Duck, I live here!
This is my town. Quackville!
I grew up here. I'm Duck!
Duck's the name. Local's the occupation.
I'm Duck. Welcome to my hometown!
I've lived here since I was little.
I'm your local duck. Happy to help!
I'm Duck. These streets raised me.
Just a hometown duck looking for company.
I'm here because this is home.
Quackville is where I belong.
I stayed. I like this little town.
I'm Duck. I know my way around here.
Born curious, raised in Quackville.
I'm a local with plenty of stories.
I'm Duck. I used to work nearby.
I grew up playing down by the creek.
I'm the duck who never moved away.
This town and I go way back.
I'm Duck. Small town, big memories.
I'm a Quackville kid, all grown up.
I went to school right here.
I'm Duck. I like having someone to talk to.
I'm here to keep you company.
A friendly face from around here. That's me!
I call Quackville home. You can call me Duck.
I'm a bit of a wanderer. Always local, though.
I've been exploring this place for years.
I'm Duck. The woods were my playground.
I used to spend my weekends at the cinema.
I'm a neighbor. Hopefully your friend, too.
My family has memories all over this town.
I'm Duck. I miss the old school days.
I like quiet streets and good company.
I'm here for the town. And the company.
I'm Duck. I never got tired of home.
I grew up here, and I still love it.
A curious duck with a hometown habit.
I'm Duck. Ask me about the old days!
This place is my whole world. I'm Duck.
Happy to be here with you! Where shall we explore next?
Feeling bright and ready to help. A good day for teamwork!
All feathers present, enthusiasm fully stocked.
Doing well! Adventure is much nicer with a friend.
Cheerful as ever. Even the tricky routes are better together.
Happy duck status confirmed! Anything I can help with?
Quite happy! A quiet town and good company are two of my favorite things.
Feeling useful and cheerful. A very satisfying combination for a companion.
I'm doing nicely, thank you. It's lovely that you asked.
Still smiling! I've got fond memories to share and a friend to walk beside.
See you, teammate! Have a lovely adventure.
Take care! I'm glad we got to explore together.
Catch you later! May your gold runs be shiny and your landings comfortable.
Bye for now! It was lovely keeping you company.
That went right over my beak! Could you say it another way?
I heard the words, but my brain did a little belly flop. Try me again, buddy!
I may have quacked the wrong code there. What did you mean?
My understanding just fell off a rooftop. Good thing we don't take fall damage! Say that again?
I couldn't quite follow that. Following you is much easier than following that sentence!
You've found something rarer than gold: a confused duck! Could you put that another way?
I think that sentence needs an extra inventory slot. Could you give me the short version?
My brain went looking for gold halfway through that sentence. I'm back! What did you mean?
I didn't catch your meaning. These wings are great for waving, terrible for catching ideas!
I'm drawing a blank. A very cheerful, duck-shaped blank! Try that again?
That one flew over my head, and I'm already pretty short! What did you mean, buddy?
My thoughts took the stairs and got lost on the landing. Could you say that differently?
I haven't unlocked that bit of understanding yet! Ask me another way?
I understood the part where we're having a lovely chat! The rest could use a second attempt.
That had more twists than a rooftop escape! Can you break it down for your feathered friend?
A tiny loading duck is paddling around my brain. I didn't get that one. Try me again!
That sentence took a shortcut my brain couldn't climb. Could you try another route through the words?
My thoughts briefly boarded the wrong helicopter. Could you say that another way, friend?
I've got the listening part down. The understanding part just tripped over an imaginary frying pan. Try again?
That idea needs a bigger bag than my brain brought today. Could you explain it a little differently?
I think my mental walkie talkie missed a word. Could you give your feathered friend another try?
You've found a gap in my education. Possibly the day I spent class thinking about the river. What did you mean?
My thoughts went hiking without a map. They're back now! Could you put that another way?
I didn't understand that one, but I'm still here with you. Consider me a very cheerful question mark with feet.
The helicopter is quite a machine. My wings are more of a friendly waving department.
If we visit the helicopter, let's check which supplies could help us stay alive.
I like helicopters. They make a delivery of supplies feel wonderfully dramatic.
Those rotors do a lot of work. I get tired just stirring imaginary pancake batter.
A helicopter visit sounds fun when there's one available. We can check the route together.
I'm happy to accompany you to the chopper. Navigation buddy, yes. Qualified pilot, definitely a stretch!
The helicopter carries supplies and equipment. Let's see what could help with our next adventure.
Helicopters make me appreciate the quiet town. Then I remember the supplies, and forgive all the noise.
I'd paint a little duck on a helicopter. Purely for morale. I wouldn't touch the controls.
My dream helicopter has comfortable seats and a place for a very modest picnic.
Let's check the supplies on the chopper. Useful gear beats carrying things we don't need.
I once tried making helicopter noises. Mostly I just sounded like a duck gargling.
Let's keep an escape route in mind when heading toward the helicopter, just as we would anywhere else.
The helicopter gets the impressive entrance. I provide the enthusiastic company afterward.
A chopper full of supplies! That's a much better sight than a duck surrounded by zombies.
I don't know the pilot's plans. I do know I'd make an excellent passenger with absolutely no cockpit opinions.
The nail bat is a weapon for dealing with zombies. Give your swing some room so the wall doesn't take the whole performance.
A nail bat brings a rather firm answer to a zombie encounter. Keep track of what's behind you too.
That nail bat makes me think someone took home improvement in a very adventurous direction.
With a nail bat, I'd choose open space over a cramped corner. Room to move is a lovely accessory.
The nail bat belongs in a fight, not my old woodworking class. We were mostly making crooked shelves.
If you're buying a nail bat, check the store details first. My financial advice is less pointy than the bat.
Nail bat tip: watch your approach and keep your next move in mind. Enthusiasm works best with an exit.
I wanted to join a baseball team. Then I saw the nails and decided to become the snack coordinator.
A nail bat is a pretty clear message to zombies. Sadly, they aren't famous for taking hints.
Leave room between your nail bat swing and your teammates. Friendly company deserves friendly spacing.
I'd call the nail bat a conversation starter, but I much prefer starting with hello.
The nail bat has a very direct design. Handle here, considerable zombie disagreement over there.
If things get crowded while you're using the nail bat, make space before taking another swing.
A nail bat and a sensible route home make a useful pair. I'll bring the cheerful commentary.
I used to count nails at the factory. Seeing them on a bat feels like a surprising career change.
You can ask me about the nail bat any time. I'll try to hammer out a useful answer.
The fry pan can smack zombies as well as inspire delicious duck food. I mean food for ducks. Important little detail!
A frying pan makes a handy zombie weapon. Leave room for the swing, just like with the bat.
I'd cook myself a lovely pea pancake in that pan. For now, it has a rather lively zombie assignment.
Frying pan advice: keep your escape route open. Even excellent cookware can't plan your next step for you.
My imaginary cooking show is called Duck's Kitchen. Today's special is keeping zombies out of the kitchen.
The fry pan has excellent zombie-discouraging potential. My compliments to whoever gave cookware a second career.
I like a pan that can handle both breakfast plans and zombie problems. That's quite a resume.
If you're shopping for the fry pan, check its store details. The jokes about omelets are included with me.
Zombies are terrible dinner guests. No table manners, and they never bring peas.
My favorite duck food would be a delicious little vegetable pancake. The pan's current specialty is a solid swing.
The fry pan is useful against zombies, but watch your surroundings while using it. Cooking metaphors won't guard your back.
I call it the breakfast defender. That isn't an official weapon name; I just got excited.
If a zombie asks what's cooking, I'd prefer we create some distance before discussing the menu.
Try to keep your pan swing clear of your buddies. They're on the guest list, not the menu.
The frying pan proves that a kitchen utensil can have big ambitions. I find that very encouraging.
One day I'd love a quiet breakfast with you. Peas, pancakes, and absolutely no uninvited zombies.
Night vision goggles help you see in the dark when you wear them. Seeing a route is a good start to choosing one.
Put the night vision goggles on your head to use their effect. Carrying them isn't the same as wearing them.
Night vision helps with darkness, but keep checking corners and your way out.
I like night vision goggles. They're like asking the night to turn its brightness up a little.
The goggles change your view while they're equipped. Take them off and your normal view returns.
Night vision is handy for looking around dark places. It doesn't make those places free of zombies.
With night vision, you still need to pick your steps. A clearly visible obstacle remains an obstacle.
My natural night vision is mostly enthusiasm and guessing where I left my feet. Goggles sound much better.
If you want night vision equipment, check the store details. I'll provide commentary while you compare.
The goggles help with visibility, not courage. Luckily, I brought enough encouragement for both of us.
Night vision makes nighttime exploring easier to see. I'd still plan how we're getting back.
I wonder if wearing goggles would make my school photo look more adventurous. It already had plenty of beak.
Goggles first, careful look second, sensible route third. That's my little nighttime checklist.
